sentences.text: Hello and welcome to the Slow English Podcast.
Today, we will talk about Haiti.
Haiti is a Caribbean country with a rich culture,
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Haiti is on the island of Hispaniola in the Caribbean Sea.
It shares the island with the Dominican Republic.
Haiti is close to Cuba, Jamaica, and Puerto Rico.
It has mountains, coastlines, and tropical forests.
What is the capital city of Haiti?
It is the largest city in Haiti.
It is next to the sea and has markets, museums,
Other cities include Capayean in the north,
Leschis in the south, Jackmell known for art and festivals.
How many people live in Haiti?
More than 11 million people live in Haiti.
Most people live in cities or villages near the coast.
Haitians are known for their strength,
What language do people speak in Haiti?
French, used in schools, government, and newspapers.
Many people also understand a little English or Spanish,
What is the weather like in Haiti?
It is usually hot and sunny.
the rainy season from April to October,
the dry season from November to March.
Hurricanes can happen between August and October.
The name Haiti means land of high mountains,
beaches and bays, rivers, waterfalls, and forests.
It is a country of natural beauty and history.
In Haiti you can see goats, pigs, chickens,
frogs, lizards, and birds in nature,
crabs, fish, and turtles by the sea.
What do people eat in Haiti?
Haitian food is flavorful, spicy, and homemade.
What do people drink in Haiti?
Cramas a sweet drink with milk and spices
Haitian drinks are often natural and homemade.
What is life like in Haiti?
Life in Haiti can be hard,
but it is full of hope and culture.
People enjoy spending time with family,
What are some holidays and traditions in Haiti?
Easter, Christmas, and all Saints Day.
a spiritual tradition with music and rhythm.
play drums, and celebrate with joy.
Haiti was the first black republic
The Haitian flag is blue and red,
with a symbol in the center.
Haiti is famous for metal art,
This is called the Haitian diaspora.
Now you know many things about Haiti.
